hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -1}g(x)$ represents the limit of $g$ as $x$ approaches $-1$.

Although the function isn't defined at $x=-1$, the $y$-values seem to approach a distinct value as the $x$-values approach $-1$.

![The graph of function g has arrows pointing along the curve, up to the right and down to the left, to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/46ae7e8eb2a25184cfb3f536370c9fdbd44b969c)

The limit seems to be somewhere between $y=3$ and $y=4$, but slightly closer to $y=3$.

![The graph of function g has a dashed horizontal line intersecting the open circle between y = 3 and y = 4, closer to y = 3.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e918bb54882843cc7b9975d29c1e2c8266c2eea2)

question.content:
The function $g$ is defined for all real numbers except for $x=-1$.

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve. The curve starts in quadrant 2, moves downward to (negative 4, 2), and moves upward through an open circle at x = negative 1, just above y = 3.The curve ends in quadrant 1.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/99a12bb4ccc470fc01e88ee5a0ec0dc9249ea6dd)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -1}g(x)$ ?**
